title: Autonomous UUV Control for Multi-Waypoint Tracking through Distributional Reinforcement Learning
subtitle: TAQC: Truncated Adaptive Quantile Critics
intro: TAQC is an end-to-end distributional reinforcement learning approach for UUV multi-waypoint tracking. Adaptive quantile modeling, multi-critic truncation, and domain randomization are evaluated on 2D and 3D tasks, unseen trajectories, and diverse simulated seabed environments.
abstract: This work presents Truncated Adaptive Quantile Critics (TAQC) for autonomous UUV multi-waypoint tracking under uncertain underwater conditions. A learnable Fraction Proposal Network enables non-uniform return-distribution quantiles, which are incorporated into a truncated multi-critic architecture through a probability-mass-weighted critic loss. Domain randomization varies currents, hydrodynamic parameters, and initial states during training. Simulation studies on 2D and 3D waypoint tasks demonstrate improved learning and task-completion efficiency, competitive tracking accuracy, and high success rates on unseen trajectories. Additional trials explore tracking in six seabed scenarios constructed using bathymetric terrain representations.

motivation.title: Research motivation
motivation.subtitle: Why study RL-based multi-waypoint UUV control?
paragraphs: Traditional UUV path-following methods have shown good performance in various conditions. However, complex underwater environments and changing task requirements call for more adaptive control methods. Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a promising approach by learning control policies through interactions with the environment.

Conventional reinforcement learning methods, such as PPO and SAC, mainly rely on expected returns for value estimation without explicitly modeling the full return distribution, potentially overlooking return variability. In addition, some existing distributional reinforcement learning methods use fixed quantile locations, limiting their ability to represent complex return distributions. Therefore, we explore a more flexible approach to return distribution modeling to potentially improve learning efficiency and stability.

Reinforcement learning policies may overfit to training conditions, leading to performance degradation in unseen environments or tasks. Therefore, we adopt domain randomization to improve policy adaptability to environmental changes and enhance generalization across different conditions.

task.title: Task description
task.subtitle: Sequential waypoint tracking under disturbances
task.text: The UUV starts from a randomized initial region and tracks a sequence of waypoints under disturbances. When the 3D distance to the current waypoint falls below a threshold, the target switches to the next waypoint. The problem is formulated as a continuous-state, continuous-action reinforcement-learning task.

framework.title: Algorithmic framework
framework.subtitle: TAQC: Truncated Adaptive Quantile Critics
framework.summary: Building upon TQC, TAQC explicitly models the return distribution within a distributional reinforcement learning framework. Its main components include a learnable Fraction Proposal Network (FPN), multiple quantile critics, a truncation mechanism for the upper tail of the mixture distribution, and domain randomization throughout training.

components.name: End-to-end control
components.desc: End-to-end reinforcement learning directly learns the mapping from state observations to control commands through environmental interactions, reducing reliance on accurate dynamic models and simplifying controller design.

components.name: Adaptive fraction proposal
components.desc: The FPN generates non-uniform quantile fractions conditioned on each state-action pair.

components.name: Multi-critic truncation
components.desc: Quantile atoms from target critics are pooled into a mixture and the right tail is truncated to reduce overestimation.

components.name: Mass-weighted critic loss
components.desc: The critic objective is reconstructed so that each quantile term is weighted by its interval probability mass.

components.name: Domain randomization
components.desc: Ocean disturbances, hydrodynamic parameters, and initial states are randomized during training.

baselines.setting: All experiments are conducted in the bluerov2_gym environment. The 2D training task uses a circle of radius 5 m; the 3D training task uses a helix of the same radius with 30 waypoints. Each episode lasts at most 800 steps. The training budgets are 500k steps for the 2D task and 1M steps for the 3D task.

experiments.title: Experimental results and analysis
experiments.subtitle: 2D and 3D tracking, unseen trajectories, disturbance robustness, and simulated seabed scenarios

sections.title: 2D path-following experiments
sections.summary: In the 2D circular tracking task, TAQC and TQC reliably solve the task. TAQC converges more efficiently, with lower variance and fewer task-completion steps. DSAC-T occasionally reaches positive rewards without a reliably converged policy, while TIQC, SAC, and PPO fail to learn a consistently successful policy under the tested disturbances. TAQC achieves competitive tracking accuracy while requiring fewer steps to complete the task than TQC.

sections.title: 3D path-following experiments
sections.summary: For 3D helical waypoint tracking, TAQC and TQC converge to positive returns, with TAQC generally learning faster and more consistently. TIQC exhibits greater variability, DSAC-T learns more slowly, and SAC/PPO do not converge satisfactorily. The tabulated comparison shows TAQC has the lowest ATE and ARE and the fewest evaluation steps among the methods able to reliably complete the task.

sections.title: 3D generalization experiments
sections.summary: The learned 3D policy is evaluated on six previously unseen paths: S-shape, double helix, polyline, figure-eight, conical helix, and comb scanning. TAQC succeeds on all six path families at high rates, whereas several distributional RL baselines encounter low or zero success rates on specific trajectories.
notes: TAQC success rates on the six trajectories are 100%, 100%, 100%, 100%, 100%, and 98%, respectively.
TQC, TIQC, and DSAC-T show failures or substantially reduced success rates on some unseen trajectories.

sections.title: Robustness with domain randomization
sections.summary: On the challenging comb-scanning task, the paper compares TAQC trained with and without domain randomization over five increasingly difficult disturbance settings. With domain randomization, the controller generally maintains higher success rates and lower tracking errors as disturbances intensify.

sections.title: Seabed terrain tracking demonstrations
sections.summary: The trained TAQC policy is further evaluated in six simulated seabed scenarios with varying terrain geometry and trajectory depth. The representative demonstrations illustrate tracking along prescribed three-dimensional trajectories (Fig. 16 of the manuscript).

terrain.title: Bathymetric terrain representation
terrain.subtitle: Seabed environments constructed from GEBCO 2025 bathymetry
paragraphs: GEBCO 2025 bathymetric data from 15.8266°–16.9246° N and 111.4766°–112.5746° E in the South China Sea are used to construct diverse simulated seabed environments.

Representative bathymetric regions are spatially rescaled to local 50 m × 50 m workspaces while preserving characteristic elevation variations. Additional synthetic terrain features increase geometric diversity for trajectory-tracking evaluation.
